semantic_sketch.normalized_claim: For every integer n with n > 1, for every real t with (n - 1) / n <= t < 1, and for every integer k with 1 <= k <= n, the floor of k times t equals k minus 1.
quantifier_order: for all integers n with n > 1
for all real numbers t with (n - 1) / n less than or equal to t and t less than 1
for all integers k with 1 less than or equal to k and k less than or equal to n

witness_dependencies: There are no existential witnesses; the claim is entirely universal over n, t, and k.
The allowed values of t depend on n through the lower bound (n - 1) / n.

payload.statement_nl: For every integer n>1 and every real number t with (n-1)/n <= t < 1, one has floor(k*t) = k-1 for every integer k with 1 <= k <= n.

result_payload.proof_nl:
Let n>1 be an integer, and let t be a real number with (n-1)/n <= t < 1. Fix an integer k with 1 <= k <= n. We show that floor(k t) = k-1.

Since t < 1 and k > 0, we have k t < k.
Also,

k t >= k(n-1)/n = k - k/n.

Because k <= n, we have k/n <= 1, hence k - k/n >= k-1. Therefore

k-1 <= k t < k.

Now k-1 is an integer, and by the defining property of the floor function, if an integer m satisfies m <= y < m+1 then floor(y)=m. Applying this with y = k t and m = k-1 gives

floor(k t) = k-1.

Since k was arbitrary, the conclusion holds for every integer k with 1 <= k <= n.
result_payload.proof_summary: Use the bounds (n-1)/n <= t < 1 to show k-1 <= kt < k for each 1<=k<=n, then apply the defining property of the floor function.

used_external_facts: Definition of floor: if an integer m satisfies m <= y < m+1, then floor(y)=m.
